title: Edge-anchored idempotency ledger and reconciliation playbook for usage accounting
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements an "edge-anchored idempotency ledger" and accompanying reconciliation playbook to prevent duplicate billing from at-least-once ingestion patterns (client retries, edge timeouts, cross-region failover). The goal is to ensure usage accounting (metering, quotas, rate limiting) remains correct even when requests are retried or replayed by clients or network components.

Background & failure modes:
- We observe rare but high-cost duplicates when clients retry through different edge proxies or when a regional failover resubmits inflight requests.
- Current ingestion is optimistic: tokens are consumed on successful write paths but there is no durable short-lived ledger at the edge that survives client proxy retries. This leads to double-counting in consumption ledger and downstream billing.
- Existing mitigation (client-side tokens alone) is insufficient because some SDKs/clients do not pass tokens consistently and some proxies rewrite headers.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Edge-anchored ledger: every edge gateway (region/replica) will create an append-only, short-lifetime ledger for idempotency tokens. On first-seen Idempotency token, the edge writes a ledger entry (token hash, first_seen_ts, proto, route, estimated_units, origin) into a regional low-latency store (Redis cluster with AOF persistence). Entries are TTL'd (configurable, default 7 days). The ledger is the first line of defense against duplicates within the TTL.

2) Two-phase commit-ish consumption commit: ingestion returns a provisional receipt (ingest-token + lease-window). Final consumption (the record that increments customer usage) is only committed once work completes or after an explicit commit API is called. This separates ingestion acceptance from billing commit and allows retries of ingestion without immediate double-billing.

3) Idempotency token format & validation: SDKs and API clients should supply Idemp-Token (client-generated UUID v4 or SDK-nonce) and optional Idemp-Version header. The edge normalizes tokens (hashing + canonicalization) to avoid header rewriting attacks. Servers reject tokens missing required entropy if billing-sensitive.

4) Reconciliation playbook: periodic reconciliation job compares the edge-ledger with the central consumption ledger and resolves 3 classes of anomalies: duplicates (same token committed twice), orphan provisos (ingested but never committed after lease expiry), and missing finalization (committed without ingest record). The reconciliation job produces compensating adjustments for billing with human review if adjustments exceed threshold.

5) Fallback & rollout controls: feature gated per-customer. For legacy customers we continue existing behavior. We provide toggle to operate in "observe-only" mode (detect duplicates but do not adjust billing) for the first rollout waves.

6) Security considerations: tokens are hashed at write time with HMAC using KMS-managed key to avoid storing raw client nonces. Edge->central reconciliation occurs over authenticated channels; reconciliation artifacts are encrypted at rest and logged.

Storage and scale tradeoffs:
- Use regional Redis clusters (already in billing infra) for hot ledger. Redis writes are idempotent by token key, enabling fast dedupe checks.
- A durable append-only ingestion index in Spanner/Postgres will store committed receipts for legal/audit requests and long-term reconciliation (retention 365 days).
- TTL selection balances memory usage vs window for safe dedupe; default 7 days chosen to cover delayed commits but can be tuned per-customer.

API/contract changes:
- New headers: Idemp-Token, Idemp-Version, Idemp-Client-Time (optional).
- Ingest response returns: 202 Accepted + "ingest_receipt" and "lease_expires_at" when provisioning.
- Commit endpoint: POST /v1/usage/commit {ingest_receipt} or SDK convenience call.

Telemetry & alarms:
- New metrics: billing_duplicates_detected, dedupe_hit_rate, orphan_ingests, reconciliation_adjustments_amount_usd, duplicate_rate_by_customer.
- Dashboards: per-customer duplicate rate, reconciler errors, and a high-severity alarm when duplicate revenue delta exceeds $50k in 24h.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for edge write + hash canonicalization, property tests for token collisions.
- Chaos testing: simulate edge restart, network partitions, and token replay across proxies.
- Load test: synthetic workload with 10% retry rate and verify dedupe-hit rate and latency impact.
- Beta rollout: internal teams -> pilot customers (low risk) -> opt-in customers -> default on for new signups -> global enablement.

Operational runbook (short):
- If reconciliation shows >0.5% duplicates for a customer over 24h: flip to observe-only and open incident.
- For edge Redis OOMs: increase eviction priority for dedupe keys, enable emergency TTL shortening, and fail closed to reject duplicates instead of over-billing.

Migration & backfill:
- Backfill agent to scan last 7 days of ingestion traces to populate edge-ledger for slow start. This will reduce initial reconciliation noise.

Open design questions / tradeoffs:
- Ledger TTL: 7 days vs 30 days. Longer reduces reconciliation complexity but increases Redis footprint and cost.
- Synchronous commit latency: the commit step adds protocol complexity and a small tail latency; can we optimize by piggybacking commit on existing completion hooks?
- Handling customers who cannot supply tokens: provide server-generated tokens (with client correlation) and flag their accounts for higher reconciliation scrutiny.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deduplication reduces duplicate-billing incidents by >=95% in pilot customers.
- Reconciler produces compensating adjustments < 0.1% of total billed amount in steady state.
- No more than 5% tail increase in p99 latency for ingest path with feature enabled.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Priya Kapoor: RFC posted to Confluence, requested feedback from Billing/Platform/SDK teams. Link in attachments.

2026-02-20 - Diego Marquez: Design review notes: prefer HMAC hashing at edge, ensure KMS rotation does not invalidate dedupe keys. Raised concern about cross-region token collisions. Suggested adding origin route metadata.

2026-03-02 - Marcus Li: Prototype implemented using regional Redis cluster (dedupe:key -> JSON metadata). Initial perf tests show 0.6ms median additional latency, p99 +2.1ms under load. Added unit tests for canonicalization.
2026-03-06 - QA (Olivia Chen): Started e2e tests with retry storms. Observed a small number of orphan provisos; increased default lease expiry from 48h to 7d for the pilot to reduce noise.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Li: Reconciliation job skeleton ready. Produces daily report with duplicate candidates and suggested adjustments. Running in observe-only against internal accounts this week.
2026-03-12 - Product (Diego Marquez): Approved pilot with two internal teams and one small external customer. Agreed to financial guardrails and manual-review thresholds.
2026-03-13 - Security (Aisha Rahman): Security review kickoff. Confirmed HMAC + KMS approach acceptable; requested threat modeling notes for token leakage scenarios.
